issue.title: HandleExitCoder does not see an ExitCoder wrapped with %w
issue.body:
### What happened

`HandleExitCoder` looks for an `ExitCoder` (and for a `MultiError`) with a **bare type assertion**, so an exit error that has been wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("%w")` is not recognised. Nothing calls `OsExiter` and nothing is written to `ErrWriter`; the process then exits with the default code `1`.

```go
cmd.Action = func(ctx context.Context, cmd *cli.Command) error {
    return fmt.Errorf("deploy failed: %w", cli.Exit("galactic perimeter breach", 9))
}
```

Running that command prints nothing, and the exit code is `1` instead of `9`.

### Why it matters

`Exit` documents that the underlying error stays reachable through the standard wrapping helpers, and `exitError` implements `Unwrap()` (that is what #1090 and #2444 added). Adding context to an `Action` error with `%w` is the ordinary way to do it, and the only consumer of that promise — `HandleExitCoder` — did not follow.

The same happens inside a `MultiError`: the last exit code is read with a bare assertion, so `newMultiError(errors.New("wowsa"), fmt.Errorf("...: %w", Exit("boom", 11)))` exits with `1` instead of `11`.

### Expected

A wrapped `ExitCoder` should be handled exactly like an unwrapped one: the message goes to `ErrWriter`, `OsExiter` is called, and the exit code is preserved.

### Environment

`urfave/cli` v3 (`main`), Go 1.27.1 on Windows. Reproduced on 2026-10-19.
